concepts.learning_objective: Explain the constitutional basis of the budget and why it is split into revenue and capital accounts.
Distinguish public goods from private goods using non-rivalry and non-excludability, and public provision from public production.
Identify the allocation, redistribution and stabilisation functions of the government budget.
Classify revenue receipts into tax and non-tax revenue and describe progressive and proportional taxation.
Identify capital receipts as those that create liabilities or reduce financial assets, debt creating or non-debt creating.
Identify revenue expenditure and its main items such as interest, defence, subsidies, salaries and grants.
Identify capital expenditure as spending that creates assets or reduces financial liabilities.
State the purpose of the three fiscal policy statements laid with the budget under the FRBMA.

topics.title: Balanced, surplus and deficit budgets; measures of deficit

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish balanced, surplus and deficit budgets.
Compute the revenue deficit and interpret its implications for government dissaving.
Compute fiscal and primary deficits and interpret them as measures of borrowing requirement.
Calculate the government expenditure multiplier and the change in equilibrium income with lump-sum taxes.
Calculate and compare the tax, transfer and balanced budget multipliers.
Analyse how proportional taxes reduce the multiplier and act as automatic stabilisers.

topics.title: Government debt, deficit reduction, FRBMA and GST

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate perspectives on the burden of debt, including Ricardian equivalence and crowding out.
Explain ways of reducing deficits and the main features of the FRBMA, 2003.
Explain how GST works as a destination-based value-added tax that removes cascading.
